minor.issue: GoogleSessionPayload.session_id has min_length=8, so short ids return 422 instead of 401. /app/auth_testing.md documents `-d '{"session_id":"nope"}'` and says 'expect 401' - the doc/curl example is wrong (returns 422). Update the playbook (or relax the constraint) so future agents don't read it as a bug.

/app/auth_testing.md claims 'cookie fallback also supported', but current_user() only accepts the Bearer access token; a request with only the session_token cookie returns 401/403 (verified). The documented Playwright happy-path (set httpOnly session_token cookie -> goto / -> lands in workspace) therefore cannot work; App.js also only checks localStorage. Either implement the cookie fallback or correct the doc.

ui_bugs.issue: vexor-mascot.png is saved as RGB (no alpha channel, near-black background) and .hero-mascot uses z-index:3 / position:absolute over .signal-card (z-index:2). Result: a visible black square overlaps the signal card and hides part of 'Uma sala para cada conversa.' Same flat black box shows in the auth aside.

Review request states data-testid=google-auth-button should be visible on '/'; it is NOT on Landing (count 0) - it only exists in screens/Auth.js. Landing also declares an unused `onGoogle` prop that App.js never passes (dead prop).

integration_issues.issue: POST /api/auth/google/session is fired TWICE for one session_id (verified: two identical request bodies captured). Cause: index.js wraps the app in React.StrictMode and GoogleCallback's useEffect only sets a `cancelled` flag - it never aborts the in-flight request. If the Emergent session_id is single-use, the second exchange will 401 and the user is pushed to the auth screen even though the first exchange succeeded. Guard with a module/ref-level 'already exchanged' flag or an AbortController.

The hash is only read once in App.js useEffect([]); there is no hashchange listener, so a hash-only navigation to /#session_id=... inside an already-loaded SPA silently stays on Landing (reproduced). Real Emergent redirect does a full load so the production path works - low risk, but worth a hashchange listener.

action_items: De-duplicate the Google session exchange in GoogleCallback (StrictMode fires the effect twice -> two POST /api/auth/google/session with the same session_id; a single-use session_id would make the second call 401 and bounce a legitimately logged-in user to /auth).
Export the mascot with a transparent background (or lower .hero-mascot z-index / move it out of the signal-card overlap) - currently an opaque black square covers hero copy.
Decide the Google entry point: either add the google-auth-button to Landing (and wire the unused onGoogle prop) or update the spec; today it exists only on the Auth screen.
Fix /app/auth_testing.md: the 'nope' curl returns 422 (session_id min_length=8) and /auth/me has NO cookie fallback, so the documented cookie-only Playwright path is invalid.
critical_code_review_comments: App.js split is good (80 lines root, screens 40-222 lines each, server.py 746 lines) - no file exceeds the 700-line guidance except server.py which is borderline.

google_session() creates a community/channel/membership for brand-new Google users but does not check the free-tier community limit path used elsewhere - keep the creation logic in one shared helper with register() to avoid drift.

google_session() links by email alone: an existing password account is silently converted to a Google-linked account (auth_provider preserved, verified forced true). Acceptable for this app but should be an explicit product decision/log.
GoogleCallback's `cancelled` flag does not abort the fetch - use AbortController so the StrictMode duplicate request is cancelled, not just ignored.
response.set_cookie(..., samesite='none', secure=True) is correct for the preview domain; note the cookie is never read by the backend (no cookie auth path), so it is currently write-only state.
